name: ath_ant_comb_scan
prose: Per-received-frame step of the ath9k antenna-diversity combining algorithm (antenna.c:721-849; the slice shows only its tail). It derives the current/main antenna from rs->rs_rssi_ctl[2], picks antcomb->ant_ratio/ant_ratio2 from whether the alt RSSI is at least low_rssi_thresh, accumulates packet count, RSSI totals and main/alt receive counters only when both main and alt RSSI are positive, updates the debug counters and runs ath_ant_short_scan_check. It returns immediately, changing nothing further, if fewer than ATH_ANT_DIV_COMB_MAX_PKTCOUNT packets have been counted (or rs->rs_moreaggr is set) and no short scan is due. Otherwise it computes the alt ratio and the main/alt average RSSI (when total_pkt_count is non-zero), reads the hardware configuration and increments antcomb->count; when count reaches ATH_ANT_DIV_COMB_MAX_COUNT it sets alt_good (calling ath_lnaconf_alt_good_scan if alt_ratio exceeds ant_ratio), resets count and sets scan and scan_not_start. When no scan is active it tries ath_ant_try_switch (if that returns true it skips to the end), and also skips to the end if alt_rssi_avg is below main_rssi_avg plus lna1_lna2_delta. Otherwise it either runs ath_ant_try_scan, or, if scan_not_start is set, either (alt not good) clears scan_not_start and sets main/alt LNA to the current main LNA's pairing, or selects the antenna from the quick scan and increments quick_scan_cnt. Every path that got past the early return reaches the end block, which applies fast diversity bias, writes the configuration with ath9k_hw_antdiv_comb_conf_set, updates debug stats, sets scan_start_time to jiffies and zeroes total_pkt_count, the main/alt RSSI totals and the main/alt receive counts.
note: [rev:n/a] only mechanical reviewers; real function ath_ant_comb_scan (antenna.c:721); the old prose said every path reaches the done label, but there is an early return at 768-770 before it

name: ar5008_hw_ani_control_new
prose: Applies one ANI (adaptive noise immunity) control command on AR5008-family hardware (ar5008_phy.c:953-1135) and returns a bool. It switches on (cmd & ah->ani_function). For ATH9K_ANI_OFDM_WEAK_SIGNAL_DETECTION it rewrites the SFCORR/SFCORR_LOW/SFCORR_EXT threshold fields (INI defaults when param is non-zero, fixed 'off' values otherwise) and sets or clears USE_SELF_CORR_LOW; for ATH9K_ANI_FIRSTEP_LEVEL it writes FIND_SIG firstep fields with level*2; for ATH9K_ANI_SPUR_IMMUNITY_LEVEL it writes the CYCPWR_THR1 fields with (level+1)*2 and (level+1)*2-1. In these three cases the registers are written every time; the logging of the change, the matching ast_ani_* statistic and the update of the stored aniState value (ofdmWeakSigDetect, firstepLevel, spurImmunityLevel) happen only when the new value differs from the stored one. ATH9K_ANI_MRC_CCK only executes WARN_ON(1). For any other masked value it logs 'invalid cmd' and returns false without touching registers or state. After the three supported cases and MRC_CCK it logs the ANI parameters and returns true.

name: ar9002_hw_init_cal
prose: Initial calibration for AR9002-family chips (ar9002_calib.c:845-935). Returns false, before PA/NF calibration and before touching cal_list, if on AR9271 ar9285_hw_cl_cal fails or on AR9285 rev 1.2+ ar9285_hw_clc fails, or, for other chips, if the AGC offset calibration does not clear AR_PHY_AGC_CONTROL_CAL within AH_WAIT_TIMEOUT. In that last case the AGC CAL bit stays set, and on AR_SREV_9280_20_OR_LATER chips AR_PHY_AGC_CONTROL_FLTR_CAL stays set and, unless AR_SREV_9287_11_OR_LATER, AR_PHY_ADC_CTL_OFF_PWDADC stays cleared (not restored). On those other chips the AGC calibration is started by setting AR_PHY_AGC_CONTROL_CAL; the FLTR_CAL set/clear and the OFF_PWDADC clear/set steps around it are done only on AR_SREV_9280_20_OR_LATER chips (OFF_PWDADC additionally not on 9287 1.1+), and on timeout-free completion they are reverted. On success it does PA calibration (ar9002_hw_pa_cal), loads the noise floor, starts NF calibration and sets cal_list, cal_list_last and cal_list_curr to NULL. For AR9100 or AR9160 1.0+ (and later) it then sets ah->supp_cals to IQ_MISMATCH_CAL, plus ADC_GAIN_CAL and ADC_DC_CAL from AR9160 1.0 on, minus ADC_GAIN_CAL on AR9287; it inserts the ADC-gain, ADC-DC and IQ calibration entries into cal_list for those that ar9002_hw_is_cal_supported accepts for the channel, points cal_list_curr at the first entry and resets it if the list is non-empty. Finally it clears ah->caldata->CalValid if ah->caldata is non-NULL and returns true.

name: ar9002_hw_get_isr
prose: Reads and decodes the AR9002 interrupt status into *masked (ar9002_mac.c:32-209; masked must be non-NULL, sync_cause_p may be NULL). Non-AR9100: it reads the async cause and, only if the MAC IRQ bit is set and the RTC reports on, reads AR_ISR; it reads the sync cause masked with AR_INTR_SYNC_DEFAULT; it sets *masked = 0 and returns false if both are zero. AR9100: it sets *masked = 0 and reads AR_ISR. If isr is non-zero: for BCNMISC it decodes AR_ISR_S2 into TIM/DTIM/DTIMSYNC/CABEND/GTT/CST/TSFOOR bits (and, without the RAC capability, writes ISR_S2 back and clears BCNMISC from isr); with RAC capability isr is re-read from AR_ISR_RAC; if isr is 0xffffffff it sets *masked = 0 and returns false (the sync cause is then neither reported nor cleared); otherwise *masked = isr & ATH9K_INT_COMMON, plus ATH9K_INT_RX for RX bits, ATH9K_INT_TX for TX bits (reading S0/S1, writing them back without RAC, and setting ah->intr_txqs) and the BCNMISC-derived bits. On non-AR9100 chips with the generic-timer bit it reads ISR_S5, sets ah->intr_gen_timer_trigger and _thresh, adds GENTIMER and TIM_TIMER bits to *masked as applicable and writes S5 back without RAC. Without RAC it writes the remaining isr back to AR_ISR. On AR9100 it then returns true (even if isr was zero). On other chips, if the sync cause is non-zero it stores it in *sync_cause_p (if non-NULL), adds ATH9K_INT_FATAL for HOST1_FATAL, HOST1_PERR or RADM_CPL_TIMEOUT (the latter also pulses AR_RC_HOSTIF in AR_RC), clears the sync cause in AR_INTR_SYNC_CAUSE_CLR; it returns true.

name: ar9003_hw_power_control_override
prose: Programs open-loop power-control and temperature-slope registers for a frequency on AR9003 chips (ar9003_eeprom.c:4803-4954; the slice shows only its second half). It writes correction[0] to the chain-0 OLPC gain delta (chains 1 and 2 only if the TX chain mask has them), sets the error-estimation mode field to 3 on the corresponding chains, then derives temp_slope: below 4000 MHz from modalHeader2G.tempSlope; otherwise on AR9550 by interpolating three EEPROM extension tables at 5180/5500/5785 MHz (giving temp_slope, temp_slope1, temp_slope2), else if miscConfiguration bit 0x20 is set by 8-point interpolation over the 5 GHz cal piers, else if base_ext2.tempSlopeLow is non-zero by 3-point interpolation, else modalHeader5G.tempSlope. For AR9550, AR9531 and AR9561 it writes the alpha-therm field per chain selected by the TX mask: when the EEPROM featureEnable bit 0 is set it writes the per-chain slopes (2 GHz: tempSlopeLow, temp_slope, tempSlopeHigh; 5 GHz: temp_slope, temp_slope1, temp_slope2, where the last two stay 0 unless the AR9550 branch computed them), otherwise it writes 0 to those chains. For other chips it writes temp_slope to AR_PHY_TPC_19; on AR9462 2.0 or later it also writes temp_slope to the TPC_19_B1 field. Finally it writes temperature[0] to the AR_PHY_TPC_18 therm-cal-value field. It returns nothing and does not use the voltage argument.

name: ar9003_hw_rtt_restore
prose: Restores the RTT (radio retention) calibration data for a channel (ar9003_rtt.c:206-258). It returns false at once, touching no hardware, if ah->caldata is NULL. If SW_PKDET_DONE is set in caldata->cal_flags it writes caldata->caldac[0] and [1] to the 2 GHz or 5 GHz (per IS_CHAN_2GHZ) CALDAC override fields of the RXRF AGC registers of chains 0 and 1 and sets the AGC_OVERRIDE bit on both chains. It then returns false if RTT_DONE is not set (this return skips the steps below). Otherwise it enables RTT, sets the restore mask to 0x30 when SW_PKDET_DONE is set and to 0x10 otherwise (both before asking for the RF bus), and calls ath9k_hw_rfbus_req; if that fails it logs an error and sets the result to false, otherwise it loads the RTT history and takes the result from ar9003_hw_rtt_force_restore. In both of those cases it then calls ath9k_hw_rfbus_done, then ar9003_hw_rtt_disable, and returns the result.
note: [rev:wrong] r15 (fail path disables RTT before ath9k_hw_rfbus_done, not after) wrong: ar9003_rtt.c:255-256 calls rfbus_done first and rtt_disable second on both paths; r1 (enable/set_mask before rfbus_req, final disable omitted) was about older prose, current prose matches 238-257

name: ath9k_hw_init_btcoex_hw
prose: Initialises the cached Bluetooth-coexistence register values in ah->btcoex_hw (btcoex.c:58-110; the slice cut the head; returns nothing). It uses a fixed configuration (slotted BT mode, txstate/txframe extend, quiet collision, priority time 2, hold-rx-clear true, wl_active_time and wl_qc_time 0x20), with rxclear polarity inverted on AR_SREV_9300_20_OR_LATER. On AR_SREV_SOC chips it sets first_slot_time to 0x1d and time_extend to 0xa (otherwise 5 and 0), assigns bt_coex_mode3 from wl_active_time and wl_qc_time (bt_coex_mode3 is not touched on other chips) and assigns bt_coex_mode2 = AR_BT_PROTECT_BT_AFTER_WAKEUP | AR_BT_PHY_ERR_BT_COLL_ENABLE (discarding its old value). For all chips it then sets bt_coex_mode to (old bt_coex_mode & AR_BT_QCU_THRESH) ORed with the new fields and qnum encoded in AR_BT_QCU_THRESH, so the old QCU-threshold bits are kept and ORed with qnum rather than replaced, while all other old bits are dropped; and it ORs the hold-rx-clear bit, ATH_BTCOEX_BMISS_THRESH in AR_BT_BCN_MISS_THRESH and AR_BT_DISABLE_BT_ANT into bt_coex_mode2 (keeping its previous value on non-SoC chips). It does not write hardware registers.

name: ath_chanctx_set_next
prose: Switches the ath9k driver from sc->cur_chan to sc->next_chan (channel.c:1222-1315; the slice cut the head). It takes sc->chan_lock with spin_lock_bh and returns without changes, with the lock released, if sc->next_chan is NULL or if force is false and ath_chanctx_defer_switch(sc) returns true. If cur_chan differs from next_chan it marks cur_chan stopped, drops the lock, notes the time if the next context is the offchannel one, stops the current context's queues, flushes all queues, sends a power-save frame (flushing the VO queue if that was sent), sets send_ps, retakes the lock, and, if cur_chan is not the offchannel context, records its TSF timestamp and value. (If cur_chan equals next_chan none of this is done.) Under the lock it then makes next_chan the current one (cur_chan = next_chan, stopped = false, next_chan = NULL), zeroes sched.offchannel_duration unless an offchannel change is pending, sets sched.state to ATH_CHANCTX_STATE_IDLE unless it is ATH_CHANCTX_STATE_FORCE_ACTIVE (in which case it is left alone), and releases the lock. If the chip is in full sleep or the current chandef differs from the new context's chandef it calls ath_set_channel (recording the channel switch time if measured) and does not wake the queues itself; otherwise it wakes the old context's queues if they were stopped. If send_ps is set it sends the power-save-off frame. In all cases that got this far it finally calls ath_offchannel_channel_change and ath_chanctx_event(ATH_CHANCTX_EVENT_SWITCH).
note: [rev:wrong] r15 (sched.state set IDLE only when FORCE_ACTIVE, reversed) wrong: channel.c:1285-1286 sets IDLE when state != FORCE_ACTIVE; r1 (acquires chan_lock itself; no stop/mark when cur==next) right and already reflected; slice cut head, real body 1222-1315

name: ath_chanctx_event
prose: State machine of the ath9k channel-context scheduler (channel.c:489-770; the slice cut the head). It sets avp from vif when vif is non-NULL (avp stays NULL otherwise and is dereferenced by BEACON_PREPARE and AUTHORIZED), takes sc->chan_lock with spin_lock_bh, handles ev and releases the lock at the single exit (there is no early return). BEACON_PREPARE: clears avp->offchannel_duration and any one-shot NoA; if avp->chanctx is not sc->cur_chan it stops there. Otherwise it may set next_chan to the offchannel context (offchannel_pending and not wait_switch) or to the next active context (state IDLE) and move to WAIT_FOR_BEACON (also from WAIT_FOR_TIMER, or when mgd_prepare_tx), clears a stale NoA when the next context is inactive and the state is not WAIT_FOR_BEACON, and if the state is not WAIT_FOR_BEACON it stops. When WAIT_FOR_BEACON it sets beacon_pending, next_tbtt, switch_start_time = next_tbtt + beacon_interval/4 and cur_chan->last_beacon, and then programs an offchannel NoA if next_chan is the offchannel context, else handles beacon-miss, sets a one-shot NoA when mgd_prepare_tx is set, else clears a wrapped noa_duration and starts a periodic NoA when the next context is active and no NoA is set or force_noa_update is set (clearing that flag). BEACON_SENT: nothing if no beacon is pending; else clears beacon_pending, and if mgd_prepare_tx is set clears it and completes sc->go_beacon, otherwise if the state is WAIT_FOR_BEACON moves to WAIT_FOR_TIMER and arms the timer for switch_start_time. TSF_TIMER: only in WAIT_FOR_TIMER: counts a beacon miss if not switch_after_beacon and a beacon is pending, moves to SWITCH and queues chanctx_work. BEACON_RECEIVED: only with ATH_OP_MULTI_CHANNEL and cur_chan not offchannel: clears beacon_pending and beacon_miss and, unless FORCE_ACTIVE, beacon_adjust is unset or tsf_val is 0, adjusts the TBTT delta, re-arms the timer and clears beacon_adjust. AUTHORIZED: only if the state is FORCE_ACTIVE and avp->chanctx == cur_chan: state becomes IDLE and processing continues as SWITCH. SWITCH: only with ATH_OP_MULTI_CHANNEL, state not FORCE_ACTIVE, cur_chan not switch_after_beacon and not offchannel: selects next_chan, state WAIT_FOR_TIMER, clears wait_switch, computes and arms the switch timer (half a beacon interval, three times that with extend_absence, minus the channel switch time), and sets beacon_pending and beacon_adjust. ENABLE_MULTICHANNEL: unless cur_chan is offchannel or switch_after_beacon, selects next_chan and queues chanctx_work. UNASSIGN: if cur_chan is still assigned, sets state IDLE only when next_chan exists, is unassigned and is not the offchannel context; if cur_chan is unassigned it sets state IDLE, and if the next context is assigned selects it as next_chan and queues chanctx_work. ASSIGN and CHANGE do nothing.

name: ath9k_calculate_summary_state
prose: Recomputes the interface summary state for a channel context (main.c:1181-1274; returns nothing; the caller holds sc->mutex). It first calls ath_chanctx_check_active(sc, ctx) and returns if ctx is not sc->cur_chan; when CONFIG_ATH9K_CHANNEL_CONTEXT is enabled and ctx is the offchannel context it calls ath9k_set_offchannel_state(sc) and returns. Otherwise it wakes the chip (ath9k_ps_wakeup), gathers iter_data with ath9k_calculate_iter_data, copies hw_macaddr into common->macaddr when has_hw_macaddr, copies the mask to common->bssidmask and applies it. If naps > 0 it enables tsfadjust and sets ah->opmode to AP; otherwise it disables tsfadjust, calls ath9k_beacon_ensure_primary_slot when beacons is set, and sets the opmode to MESH_POINT, OCB, ADHOC or STATION in that order of preference (nmeshes, nocbs, nadhocs, else station). It calls ath9k_hw_setopmode, sets ctx->switch_after_beacon false, and sets ATH9K_INT_TSFOOR in ah->imask when nstations + nadhocs + nmeshes > 0; otherwise it clears the bit and sets switch_after_beacon true only if naps == 1 and iter_data.beacons. If the opmode is STATION: with a primary_sta it uses it as primary beacon vif with beacons = true, calls ath9k_set_assoc_state(sc, primary_sta, changed) and records ctx->primary_sta; without one it clears ctx->primary_sta, zeroes common->curbssid and curaid, writes the association id and, when MCI is enabled, updates the WLAN channels. It then sets sc->nbcnvifs, configures beacons, sets the interrupt mask, updates ah->slottime and calls ath9k_hw_init_global_settings if the slot time changed, sets or clears ATH_OP_PRIM_STA_VIF according to primary_sta, logs the MAC/BSSID/mask with ath_dbg, and calls ath9k_ps_restore.

name: ath_isr
prose: Hard interrupt handler of ath9k (real name ath_isr, main.c:488-603; the listed name ath9k_interrupt does not exist). dev is the ath_softc. It returns IRQ_NONE, before any hardware access, if sc->sc_ah is NULL or ATH_OP_INVALID is set (note ath9k_hw_common(ah) is computed before the NULL test), and IRQ_NONE if ath9k_hw_intrpend reports nothing pending. It then calls ath9k_hw_getisr, which reads and clears the hardware interrupt status (and the sync cause, which is passed to the debug code), and masks the status with ah->imask. If ATH_OP_HW_RESET is set it kills the hardware interrupts and returns IRQ_HANDLED (the ISR has already been read at that point). If no status bits remain it returns IRQ_NONE, after the hardware status was already read and cleared. Otherwise it ORs the status into sc->intrstatus under sc->intr_lock and marks sched if any SCHED_INTR bit (FATAL, BB_WATCHDOG, RXORN, RXEOL, RX/RXLP/RXHP, TX, BMISS, CST, GTT, TSFOOR, GENTIMER, MCI) is set. A FATAL status, or BB_WATCHDOG when HW_BB_WATCHDOG hang checks are configured, skips the per-bit handling. Otherwise: SWBA schedules the beacon tasklet; TXURN raises the TX trigger level; RXEOL clears RXEOL and RXORN from ah->imask and rewrites the interrupt mask; and, if the chip lacks autosleep capability, TIM_TIMER with sc->ps_idle set (WARN once) skips the rest, while without ps_idle it wakes the chip, clears RX abort and sets PS_WAIT_FOR_BEACON under sc->sc_pm_lock. At the end, if sched is set it kills all hardware interrupts and schedules sc->intr_tq, and it returns IRQ_HANDLED.

name: ath_mci_intr
prose: Handles an AR9003 MCI (Bluetooth coexistence) interrupt (real name ath_mci_intr(sc), mci.c:485-631; the interrupt and rx-message bitmasks are read inside with ar9003_mci_get_interrupt, not passed in; returns nothing). If ar9003_mci_state(MCI_STATE_ENABLE) is 0 it initialises the GPM offset and returns. Otherwise: for RX_MSG_REQ_WAKE it sends MCI_REMOTE_RESET (16-byte payload) and MCI_SYS_WAKING, clears that bit in its local copy, resets the req-wake state and sets BT awake; for SYS_WAKING it sets BT awake if bt_state is sleep and the remote is not asleep; for SYS_SLEEPING it sets bt_state to MCI_BT_SLEEP if it was awake and the remote is not awake; for RX_INVALID_HDR or CONT_INFO_TIMEOUT it recovers RX and sets skip_gpm; for SCHD_INFO it records the last schedule message offset; for RX_MSG_GPM it loops while more GPM data is indicated: it returns immediately (without recycling or processing further messages) if ATH_OP_HW_RESET is set, stops the loop on an invalid offset, and for each message dispatches calibration messages to ath_mci_cal_msg and COEX_AGENT messages to ath_mci_msg unless skip_gpm is set, recycling every GPM it read (including skipped ones). It then clears the handled hardware-message bits from the local mask (logging CONT_INFO) and, if RX_INVALID_HDR or CONT_INFO_TIMEOUT was set, calls ath_mci_msg(sc, MCI_GPM_COEX_NOOP, NULL). Local copies of the masks are modified, not the hardware status.
note: [rev:n/a] only mechanical reviewers; real function ath_mci_intr (mci.c:485); old prose wrongly described mci_int/mci_int_rxmsg as inputs

name: carl9170_op_ampdu_action
prose: mac80211 ampdu_action callback of carl9170 (main.c:1395-1487; the slice cut the head). It returns -EOPNOTSUPP if modparam_noht is set or if the action is not one of the handled IEEE80211_AMPDU_* values. TX_START: -EOPNOTSUPP if sta_info->ht_sta is false, -ENOMEM if the carl9170_sta_tid allocation fails; otherwise it initialises the tid_info (hsn, bsn and snx from *ssn, state CARL9170_TID_STATE_PROGRESS, tid, max, sta, vif, list heads, queue, lock), links it at the tail of ar->tx_ampdu_list and increments tx_ampdu_list_len under ar->tx_ampdu_list_lock, publishes it in sta_info->agg[tid] and returns IEEE80211_AMPDU_TX_START_IMMEDIATE (not 0). TX_STOP_CONT, TX_STOP_FLUSH and TX_STOP_FLUSH_CONT: if sta_info->agg[tid] is set, under ar->tx_ampdu_list_lock it sets that tid_info->state to CARL9170_TID_STATE_SHUTDOWN only when the state was numerically greater than SHUTDOWN; it then sets sta_info->agg[tid] to NULL, calls ieee80211_stop_tx_ba_cb_irqsafe and queues ar->ampdu_work, and returns 0. TX_OPERATIONAL: sets sta_info->stats[tid].clear = true and .req = false, and if agg[tid] is non-NULL zeroes its bitmap and sets state CARL9170_TID_STATE_IDLE; if agg[tid] is NULL it issues WARN_ON_ONCE and returns -EFAULT, otherwise 0. RX_START and RX_STOP do nothing and return 0 (handled by hardware).

name: TRACE_EVENT(ath_log,
prose: Tracepoint definition for ath_log(wiphy, vaf); the TRACE_EVENT macro generates the function trace_ath_log (ath/trace.h:27). When CONFIG_ATH_TRACEPOINTS is not set the local TRACE_EVENT macro turns it into an empty static inline function. When tracing is enabled and the event is recorded, TP_fast_assign stores the module name (KBUILD_MODNAME), wiphy_name(wiphy) and the message formatted from vaf->fmt and vaf->va into the trace record; the text format prints driver, device and message. It returns nothing and does not modify its arguments; wiphy and vaf must be valid when the event is recorded.
note: [rev:n/a] only mechanical reviewers; macro-generated function (ath/trace.h:27-52)

name: wil_suspend_keep_radio_on
prose: Suspends a wil6210 device while keeping the radio on (pm.c:179-297; the slice cut the head). It tries down_write_trylock(&wil->mem_lock); on failure it increments suspend_stats.rejected_by_host and returns -EBUSY with no other change. Otherwise it sets wil_status_suspending (under the lock, then released) and stops all net queues. If TX is not idle, RX is not idle or WMI is not idle it increments suspend_stats.rejected_by_host, clears wil_status_suspending, wakes the connected net queues and returns -EBUSY; a failure of wmi_suspend takes the same reject path (-EBUSY) without incrementing that counter. It then, if NAPI is enabled, waits for RX to become idle until WIL_DATA_COMPLETION_TO_MS has passed; a timeout, or WMI events still pending afterwards, increments suspend_stats.r_on.failed_suspends and goes to the resume-after-failure path. It masks the IRQ, sets the PERST-reset-disable bit (BIT_USER_CLKS_RST_PWGD), and, if wil->platform_ops.suspend exists, calls it; on failure it increments failed_suspends, clears that bit, unmasks the IRQ and goes to the resume-after-failure path. On success it saves bus_request_kbps in bus_request_kbps_pre_suspend, sets the bus request to 0, sets wil_status_suspended, clears wil_status_suspending and returns 0. The resume-after-failure path sets wil_status_resuming, clears wil_status_suspending, calls wmi_resume and returns its error if it failed, or, if it succeeded, wakes the connected net queues and returns -EBUSY.

name: __wil_tx_vring_tso
prose: Builds a TSO (TCP segmentation offload) descriptor chain for a GSO skb on a wil6210 TX ring (txrx.c:1725-2024; the slice shows only the second half). Early returns with no ring changes: -EINVAL if the ring's txdata is not enabled, -ENOMEM if the available descriptors are fewer than nr_frags + 1, -EINVAL if skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type masked with TCPV4|TCPV6 is neither exactly TCPV4 nor exactly TCPV6 (for TCPv4 it first zeroes ip_hdr tot_len and check, for TCPv6 the payload_len, in the skb's headers) and -EINVAL if skb->ip_summed is not CHECKSUM_PARTIAL (the header zeroing has already happened by then). It then DMA-maps the headers (skb_tcp_all_headers bytes); a mapping failure returns the initial rc (-EINVAL) with nothing to undo. It then walks the linear remainder and the page fragments, mapping each piece in at most mss-sized chunks and filling descriptors, setting the first/mid/last TSO types and fragment counts; if the ring runs out of descriptors (descs_used reaches avail) it sets rc = -ENOMEM and jumps to mem_error; a mapping error or finishing with no data descriptor goes to mem_error with rc still -EINVAL. mem_error walks back over every descriptor used so far (including the header), copies it, sets TX_DMA_STATUS_DU, unmaps it and zeroes its context, then returns rc; vring->swhead is not changed and no skb reference is taken. On success it sets the last data descriptor and the total descriptor count in the header descriptor, stores skb_get(skb) in the context of the last descriptor, updates idle statistics, executes write barriers, advances swhead by descs_used, records the tx latency timestamp (or clears skb->cb), writes vring->swhead to the hardware tail and returns 0.

name: b43_radio_2057_rcal
prose: Runs the radio 0x2057 resistor calibration (RCAL) on a b43 N-PHY device and returns the result as a u8 (phy_n.c:810-919). It saves twelve PHY RF-control registers and six RF override registers, zeroes the twelve, writes 0x07ff (OVER0, OVER1, OVER3, OVER4) or 0x007f (OVER5, OVER6) to the overrides, then does radio-revision specific setup: rev 5 clears bit 1 of REV7_RF_CTL_OVER3, sets bit 0 of R2057_IQTEST_SEL_PU and sets bit 0 and clears bit 1 of R2057v7_IQTEST_SEL_PU2; rev 9 sets OVER3 and MISC_REG3 bit 1, saves R2057_IQTEST_SEL_PU and writes 0x11 to it; rev 14 saves IQTEST_SEL_PU and PU2, sets MISC_REG3 and OVER3 bit 1 and writes 0x2 to PU2 and 0x1 to PU. It then sets the RCAL enable bit (0x1), the start bit (0x2), and clears the start bit, and waits (up to 1 s, polling every 100 us) for bit 0 of R2057_RCAL_STATUS (mask 1, value 1) to become set. On timeout it logs an error and returns 0 immediately, with the enable bit still set, the start bit cleared, the saved PHY registers not restored and the revision-specific changes left in place. On success it reads R2057_RCAL_STATUS & 0x3E, clears the enable bit, restores the six override and then the twelve control registers, and by radio rev: revs 0-4 and 6 update R2057_TEMPSENSE_CONFIG (mask ~0x3C) and R2057_BANDGAP_RCAL_TRIM (mask ~0xF0, value shifted left by 2); rev 5 clears bit 0 of R2057_IPA2G_CASCONV_CORE0 and bit 1 of PU2 and does not restore R2057_IQTEST_SEL_PU (it stays with bit 0 set); rev 9 restores IQTEST_SEL_PU; rev 14 restores both; other revisions get no radio writes. It returns the masked status value (an even number in 0 to 62).

name: get_integer
prose: Static helper in b43 sysfs.c (lines 23-35) that parses a decimal integer from a sysfs write buffer. It returns -EINVAL if count is 0. Otherwise it copies at most min(count, 10) bytes of buf into a zero-initialised 11-byte local buffer (so at most 10 bytes of buf are read) and returns simple_strtol(tmp, NULL, 10) converted to int. simple_strtol accepts an optional leading '-', stops at the first non-digit and yields 0 when there are no leading digits; the long result is not saturated or range-checked before the conversion to int, so values outside the int range are truncated by the conversion, and a legitimately negative parsed value cannot be told apart from the -EINVAL error. It takes no locks and has no side effects.

name: b43_generate_txhdr
prose: Builds the b43 hardware TX header for one 802.11 fragment (xmit.c:235-568; the slice cut the head). It zeroes *txhdr, picks the main rate (from ieee80211_get_tx_rate, default 1 Mb CCK) and fallback rate, and sets phy_rate, mac_frame_ctl, tx_receiver and the fallback duration (the original duration_id if the rates are equal or duration_id is 0 or has bit 0x8000, else a computed duration). If info->control.hw_key is set it takes dev->key[hw_key_idx] (the index is only checked with B43_WARN_ON, not enforced); if that key has no keyconf it returns -ENOKEY at once, leaving the header only partly filled and the fragment not to be transmitted. Otherwise it adds the ICV length to the PLCP length, sets the key index/algorithm in mac_ctl, and copies either the TKIP phase-1 key plus three IV bytes or min(iv_len, sizeof iv) IV bytes into txhdr->iv. It then writes the main and fallback PLCP headers (layout by firmware header format 598/351/410), fallback and PHY rate flags, the channel radio code, the PHY control word (encoding, short preamble, antenna) and MAC control bits (ACK, hardware sequence, first fragment, 5 GHz). It overwrites info->control.rates[0].count with the long (and sets LONGFRAME, also for RTS/CTS use) or short retry limit. For RTS/CTS or CTS-to-self protection it generates the RTS or CTS frame into the header with its PLCP headers, fallback rate, duration and rate flags (phy_ctl1 words only for RTS and LP/N/HT PHYs). It stores the cookie by header format, fills phy_ctl1 and phy_ctl1_fb for LP, N and HT PHYs, stores the mac_ctl, phy_ctl and extra frame type words and returns 0.

name: b43legacy_radio_interference_mitigation_disable
prose: Turns off one b43legacy interference-mitigation mode (radio.c:1217-1313; static, returns nothing). Saved values are fetched from phy->interfstack by (register type, offset) key through _stack_restore, not in push order; if no entry matches, _stack_restore executes B43legacy_BUG_ON(1) and returns 0. NONWLAN with phy->rev != 1: clears bit 0x0800 of PHY 0x042B and sets bit 0x4000 of B43legacy_PHY_G_CRS; nothing is restored. NONWLAN with rev == 1: restores PHY 0x0078 (looked up as a PHY-register entry, while the enable function saved 0x0078 as a radio-register entry, so that lookup finds no match and reaches the B43legacy_BUG_ON), recalculates the NRSSI threshold, restores 0x0406, clears 0x0800 in 0x042B, clears bit 11 of PHY_RADIO_BITFIELD only if dev->bad_frames_preempt is false, sets 0x4000 in G_CRS, and restores 0x04A0, 0x04A1, 0x04A2, 0x04A8, 0x04AB, 0x04A7, 0x04A3, 0x04A9, 0x0493, 0x04AA, 0x04AC. MANUALWLAN: returns without any change if bit 0x0800 of PHY 0x0033 is clear; otherwise sets phy->aci_enable = false and restores PHY_RADIO_BITFIELD, G_CRS, 0x0033, 0x04A3, 0x04A9, 0x0493, 0x04AA, 0x04AC, 0x04A0, 0x04A7, then 0x04C0 and 0x04C1 (rev >= 2) or 0x0406, then 0x04A1, 0x04AB, 0x04A8, then for rev 2 0x04AD and 0x04AE, for rev >= 3 0x04AD, 0x0415, 0x0416, 0x0417 and ILT 0x1A02 and 0x1A03, then 0x04A2, 0x04A8 again, 0x042B and 0x048C; it clears bit 0x800 of the ucode flags in shared memory if it was set and calls b43legacy_calc_nrssi_slope. name: brcmf_cfg80211_start_ap
prose: cfg80211 start_ap callback of brcmfmac (cfg80211.c:5120-5367; the slice cut the head). It reads the current regulatory (11d) setting into ifp->vif->is_11d. If settings->ssid is NULL or empty it takes the SSID from the beacon head and returns -EINVAL if there is no SSID IE or it is longer than IEEE80211_MAX_SSID_LEN. For a non-MBSS interface it then disables MPC and ARP/ND offload and sets regulatory, beacon interval, DTIM period, (for AP role, when ifidx is 0 or neither RSDB nor MCHAN is enabled) BRCMF_C_DOWN and the INFRA mode, any failure going to exit; for an MBSS interface it instead returns -EINVAL (after WARN_ON) if 11d is supported and differs from the vif's setting. For the AP role it sets the mbss iovar (result ignored when the feature is enabled), AP mode, the chanspec (non-MBSS), brings the interface up, optionally configures PSK and SAE offload, calls brcmf_parse_configure_security, reconfigures WEP, sets the SSID and the closednet iovar; for the P2P GO role it sets the chanspec, security, the bsscfg ssid and enables the bss; each of these failures goes to exit with the negative error. For any other role it only executes WARN_ON(1) and continues. It then configures the management IEs, sets BRCMF_VIF_STATUS_AP_CREATED in sme_state and enables the carrier. At exit, if err is non-zero and the interface is not MBSS, it re-enables MPC and ARP/ND offload; it returns err. err starts as -EPERM and is overwritten by the results of the calls made, so for a non-MBSS interface with an unsupported role (after INFRA succeeded) it returns 0 with the AP_CREATED bit set and the carrier enabled, while for an MBSS interface with an unsupported role it returns -EPERM with those bits set too. On error returns before the AP_CREATED bit is set, the bit is not set; previous firmware changes are not rolled back.

name: brcms_c_update_beacon_hw
prose: Installs a beacon into the brcmsmac hardware beacon templates (main.c:7281-7328; static, returns nothing). If both MCMD_BCN0VLD and MCMD_BCN1VLD are set in the maccommand register it first writes MI_BCNTPL to macintstatus (clearing a previous status). If wlc->beacon_template_virgin is true it clears that flag, writes the beacon into both templates (brcms_c_beacon_write with bcn0 and bcn1 true), sets MCMD_BCN0VLD in maccommand (it does not clear MCMD_BCN1VLD) and returns. Otherwise it re-reads maccommand: if both valid bits are still set it sets MI_BCNTPL in wlc->defmacintmask and returns without writing a template. Otherwise, if MCMD_BCN0VLD is clear it writes only template 0 and sets MCMD_BCN0VLD; else, if MCMD_BCN1VLD is clear it writes only template 1 and sets MCMD_BCN1VLD. Each brcms_c_beacon_write call computes the PLCP for the beacon's tx rate, updates the beacon PHY tx control, writes the beacon (rounded up to 4 bytes, at most BCN_TMPL_LEN) and its length to the selected template(s), and writes the TIM position and DTIM period (or the beacon end and 0 when tim_offset is 0) to shared memory.

name: wlc_phy_cal_txiqlo_nphy
prose: Runs (or continues, in multi-phase mode) the N-PHY TX IQ/LO calibration (phy_n.c:25624-25984; the slice cut the head). It stays in carrier search, for PHY revs >= 4 saves and clears pi->phyhang_avoid, saves the RFSEQ gain table entries, sets the calibration gains per core, runs the TX calibration radio and PHY setup, loads the LOFT/IQ-imbalance ladders for the channel bandwidth (only for PHY revs below 6 and not rev 5 with iPA on 2 GHz) and then plays a tone (wlc_phy_tx_tone_nphy) or, when the multi-phase state is past TXPHASE0, samples. If the tone cannot be started its error is kept in bcmerror and the calibration loop is skipped. Otherwise it loads start coefficients (multi-phase coefficients, the previous best coefficients when !fullcal and they are valid, otherwise defaults with fullcal forced true), selects the full or recal command list by PHY revision, determines which commands to run (all, or the next pi->mphase_txcal_numcmds in multi-phase mode starting at mphase_txcal_cmdidx), and for each command writes it, waits up to 20000 us for the busy bits to clear, and copies the resulting coefficients; if the hardware is still busy it executes WARN and returns -EIO immediately, without the cleanup below (carrier search stays suspended, phyhang_avoid stays cleared on rev >= 4, the RFSEQ gain table and the radio/phy setup are not restored, playback is not stopped). After the loop it updates mphase_txcal_cmdidx (wrapping to 0), and when not in multi-phase mode or at the last phase stores the final coefficients in pi->nphy_txiqlocal_bestc with nphy_txiqlocal_coeffsvalid set and nphy_txiqlocal_chanspec updated, otherwise stores them in pi->mphase_txcal_bestcoeffs; then it stops playback. In all paths other than the -EIO return it runs the PHY and radio cleanup, restores the RFSEQ gain table, applies the tx-iq workaround on PHY rev < 2 when appropriate, restores phyhang_avoid on rev >= 4, leaves carrier search and returns bcmerror (0 or the tone error).
